title: Both coefficient shift squares for signed external chain evaluations
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal C$ a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_{\mathcal C}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $U,V$ be cochain complexes of $A$-modules and $E,H,N,M,J$ cochain complexes of these module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Write $\underline U,\underline V$ for termwise application of the constant module functor [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. Use the direct-sum tensor differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes dy$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the global Hom complex $\operatorname{Hom}^n(B,J)=\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}_{A_{\mathcal C}}(B^j,J^{j+n})$ with differential $df=d_Jf-(-1)^{|f|}fd_B$ [def-pur-hom-complex], and shifts $B[1]^q=B^{q+1}$, $d_{B[1]}=-d_B$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let
$$u:\underline U\otimes_A E\to N,\quad v:\underline V\otimes_A H\to M,\quad i:N\otimes_A M\to J$$
be arbitrary chain maps. Let $p:U\otimes_A V\to\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(E\otimes_A H,J)$ be the chain pairing
$$p(w\otimes z)(e\otimes h)=(-1)^{sq}i(u(w\otimes e)\otimes v(z\otimes h)),\qquad |w|=r,\ |z|=s,\ |e|=q.$$
Put $G=E\otimes_A H$. For any $B$, write $\theta_B:\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(B[1],J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(B,J)[-1]$ for the chain isomorphism $(\theta_Bf)^j=(-1)^nf^{j-1}$ in Hom degree $n$. Let $p_E$ be the same formula with $U,E,u$ replaced by $U[-1],E[1],u\eta_{U,E}$, where $\eta_{U,E}(w\otimes e)=(-1)^rw\otimes e$ for $w\in U[-1]^r$. Define $p_H$ similarly using $V[-1],H[1],v\eta_{V,H}$.

Let $\tau_1:U[-1]\otimes_A V\cong(U\otimes_A V)[-1]$ be the tensor-shift comparison with no sign, and $\tau_2:U\otimes_A V[-1]\cong(U\otimes_A V)[-1]$ the comparison $w\otimes z\mapsto(-1)^rw\otimes z$ for $w\in U^r$. Let $\kappa_E:E[1]\otimes_A H\cong G[1]$ have no sign and $\kappa_H:E\otimes_A H[1]\cong G[1]$ send $e\otimes h$ to $(-1)^qe\otimes h$ for $e\in E^q$. These tensor comparisons are chain isomorphisms. Define $\rho_E=\theta_G\circ\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(\kappa_E^{-1},J)$ and $\rho_H=\theta_G\circ\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(\kappa_H^{-1},J)$. Then both equalities of chain maps hold:
$$\rho_Ep_E=p[-1]\tau_1,\qquad \rho_Hp_H=p[-1]\tau_2.$$
On homogeneous sections the two sides of the first equality have the same unsigned evaluation and sign $(-1)^{sq+s}$, with $w\in U[-1]^r$, $z\in V^s$, $e\in E[1]^q$. The two sides of the second equality have the same unsigned evaluation and sign $(-1)^{sq+q+r}$, with $w\in U^r$, $z\in V[-1]^s$, $e\in E^q$. No boundedness, flatness or injectivity is assumed.

proof.text: First construct the graded pairing and fix an equality test. By the constant-module construction, an element $w\in U^r$ has a compatible constant section on every object of $\mathcal C$. Thus $u(w,-)$ and $v(z,-)$ are morphisms of graded sheaves of degrees $r$ and $s$. In bidegree $(q,t)$, the displayed formula is $A_{\mathcal C}$-balanced in $e,h$, $A$-bilinear in $w,z$, and compatible with every restriction. The presheaf-tensor and sheafification universal properties therefore extend it uniquely to $E^q\otimes H^t$, and the direct-sum universal property extends it to $G$. Its output has degree $r+s+q+t$. Taking the family of these maps over all $q+t$ defines an element of global $\operatorname{Hom}^{r+s}(G,J)$. Bilinearity then gives $p$ on $U\otimes_A V$. The same argument applies to both shifted formulas. These constructions use only finite sums in each tensor input; the Hom target is a product of component maps. Equality can be checked on each homogeneous pure tensor before sheafification: uniqueness of extension and of maps out of the direct sum then gives equality of the sheaf morphisms and all their Hom components.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose); explicit agent calculation for the displayed external pairing and shift conventions.

proof.text:
Check the differential of $p$ directly. Put $|w|=r$, $|z|=s$, $|e|=q$, $|h|=t$ and $n=r+s$. Suppress the tensor symbol inside the arguments of $u,v$ and write $I(a,b)=i(a\otimes b)$. Since $u,v,i$ are chain maps, $d_J(p(w,z)(e,h))$ has four terms, in the order obtained by differentiating $w,e,z,h$, with unsigned values
$$I(u(dw,e),v(z,h)),\ I(u(w,de),v(z,h)),\ I(u(w,e),v(dz,h)),\ I(u(w,e),v(z,dh))$$
and respective sign exponents
$$sq,\quad sq+r,\quad sq+r+q,\quad sq+r+q+s.$$
In $d_{\rm Hom}p(w,z)=d_Jp(w,z)-(-1)^n p(w,z)d_G$, the two subtracted terms have unsigned values given by differentiating $e,h$ and exponents $n+s(q+1)$ and $n+sq+q$. These equal $sq+r$ and $sq+r+q+s$ modulo $2$, so cancel the second and fourth terms. The remaining exponents $sq$ and $sq+r+q$ are exactly those of $p(dw,z)$ and $(-1)^rp(w,dz)$. Hence $d_{\rm Hom}p=p\,d_{U\otimes V}$. This calculation applies with shifted complexes as soon as the shifted evaluation maps are chain maps, as checked below.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose); explicit agent calculation for the displayed external pairing and shift conventions.

proof.text:
Verify the Hom shift comparison rather than assuming it. If $f$ has Hom degree $n$ from $B[1]$ to $J$, then $f^{j-1}:B^j\to J^{j+n-1}$, as required in degree $n$ of $\operatorname{Hom}(B,J)[-1]$. Since $d_{B[1]}=-d_B$, the $j$-component of $\theta_B(df)$ is
$$(-1)^{n+1}d_J f^{j-1}-f^j d_B^j.$$
The $j$-component of the target differential $-d_{\operatorname{Hom}(B,J)}$ applied to $(-1)^nf^{j-1}$ is the same expression. The inverse in degree $n$ sends $g^j$ to $(-1)^ng^{j+1}$ in component $j$; both composites multiply by $(-1)^{2n}=1$. Thus $\theta_B$ is a chain isomorphism for arbitrary $B,J$.

proof.text:
For $w\in U[-1]^r=U^{r-1}$ and $e\in E[1]^q=E^{q+1}$, the differential on the source of $\eta_{U,E}$ is $-dw\otimes e+(-1)^{r+1}w\otimes de$. Applying $\eta$ to these two terms gives
$$(-1)^r dw\otimes e-w\otimes de,$$
since their first-factor degrees are $r+1$ and $r$. Applying the target differential to $(-1)^rw\otimes e$ gives precisely the same two terms, because the original degree of $w$ is $r-1$. The inverse multiplies the reverse reindexed summand by $(-1)^r$, so its two composites are the identity. Replacing $(U,E,r,q)$ by $(V,H,s,t)$ proves the same assertion for $\eta_{V,H}$. Consequently $u\eta_{U,E}$ and $v\eta_{V,H}$ are chain maps. Step 2 now applies to $p_E,p_H$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose); explicit agent calculation for the displayed external pairing and shift conventions.

proof.text: Check all four tensor comparisons uniformly, on module complexes as well as module-sheaf complexes. For an integer $a$, the unsigned reindexing $X[a]\otimes Y\to(X\otimes Y)[a]$ commutes with differentials: on $x\in X[a]^k$ the two coefficients are $(-1)^a$ for $dx\otimes y$ and $(-1)^k$ for $x\otimes dy$, since $(-1)^a(-1)^{k+a}=(-1)^k$. The reindexing $X\otimes Y[a]\to(X\otimes Y)[a]$ with coefficient $(-1)^{ak}$ also commutes with differentials: the coefficients after either composition are $(-1)^{ak+a}$ on $dx\otimes y$ and $(-1)^{ak+k+a}$ on $x\otimes dy$. Both have inverses given by reverse reindexing with the same scalar. Specializing $a=-1$ gives $\tau_1,\tau_2$; specializing $a=1$ gives $\kappa_E,\kappa_H$. Precomposition by the inverse of either $\kappa$ is a Hom-complex chain isomorphism by the functoriality in the definition of Hom. Together with Step 3 this makes $\rho_E,\rho_H$ chain isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose); explicit agent calculation for the displayed external pairing and shift conventions.

proof.text: Compute the first square, keeping shifted degrees distinct. Take $w\in U[-1]^r$, $z\in V^s$, $e\in E[1]^q$, and $h\in H^t$. The original degrees of $w,e$ are $r-1,q+1$, respectively. Set $n=r+s$ and denote the common unsigned evaluation by $I=i(u(w\otimes e)\otimes v(z\otimes h))$. On the left, $p_E$ contributes $(-1)^{sq}$, $u\eta$ contributes $(-1)^r$, $\kappa_E^{-1}$ contributes no sign, and $\theta_G$ in degree $n$ contributes $(-1)^{r+s}$. The total exponent is $sq+r+r+s\equiv sq+s\pmod2$. On the right, $\tau_1$ is unsigned and the underlying unshifted $p$ evaluates $e$ in degree $q+1$, giving exponent $s(q+1)=sq+s$. Shifting a degree-zero chain map adds no scalar. Thus both sides give $(-1)^{sq+s}I$. The equality test in Step 1 proves $\rho_Ep_E=p[-1]\tau_1$ in every component, and all maps involved are chain maps by Steps 2–5.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose); explicit agent calculation for the displayed external pairing and shift conventions.

proof.text: Compute the second square separately. Take $w\in U^r$, $z\in V[-1]^s$, $e\in E^q$, and $h\in H[1]^t$. The original degrees of $z,h$ are $s-1,t+1$. Again put $n=r+s$ and $I=i(u(w\otimes e)\otimes v(z\otimes h))$. The four left-hand contributions are $sq$ from $p_H$, $s$ from $v\eta$, $q$ from $\kappa_H^{-1}$, and $r+s$ from $\theta_G$. Their sum is $sq+s+q+r+s\equiv sq+q+r\pmod2$. The right-hand contributions are $r$ from $\tau_2$ and $(s-1)q$ from the unshifted $p$. Since $r+(s-1)q\equiv sq+q+r\pmod2$, both sides give $(-1)^{sq+q+r}I$. Step 1 extends this to equality of all components, proving $\rho_Hp_H=p[-1]\tau_2$. All formulas and cancellations hold for every integer degree, including negative degrees, and only use the tensor, Hom and shift differentials. No boundedness, flatness or injectivity enters.
